initialFiles.content:
# Retry policy contract

Implement src/retry-policy.mjs export decideRetry(input). This is a pure decision function; it must not call fetch, timers, clocks, or mutate input.

Input: method (case-insensitive string), status (HTTP integer or absent), errorName (string or absent), aborted (boolean), attempt (failed attempt number, positive integer starting at 1), retryAfter (string or absent), nowMs (finite injected epoch milliseconds).
Output exactly { retry: boolean, delayMs: number, reason: string }.

Apply these rules in this order:
1. aborted=true or errorName='AbortError' => false,0,'canceled'.
2. Any method except GET and HEAD => false,0,'unsafe-method'.
3. attempt>=3 => false,0,'exhausted' (at most 3 total attempts).
4. Retry only status 429 or 503; when status is absent, retry TypeError or TimeoutError. Everything else => false,0,'not-retryable'.
5. Retry delay defaults to 250 * 2 ** (attempt-1). Retry-After may replace that delay when it is an all-digit non-negative integer seconds or an IMF-fixdate HTTP-date (e.g. Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT). Whitespace may surround a value. Reject decimal, signed, arbitrary Date.parse-accepted text, overflow and invalid dates and use default. A past valid date gives zero delay. Clamp valid delay to at most 5000ms.
6. Retrying returns true,computed-delay,'transient'.

Attempts and nowMs passed by the service satisfy the input contract. The 3-attempt limit, GET/HEAD-only allowlist, 250ms base, 5s cap and no jitter are local business policy, not universal HTTP requirements.
